walkthroughs.body_html:
Oliver Cromwell was a Puritan MP from Huntingdon.

He had little military training, but he was a natural leader. He trained a cavalry unit called the Ironsides — strong, fast and very disciplined.

His men prayed, sang psalms and did not drink before battle. 🐎

walkthroughs.h2: Marston Moor and the New Model Army
walkthroughs.body_html:
In July 1644, Parliament and the Scots beat the king's forces at the Battle of Marston Moor near York. Cromwell's cavalry was key.

In 1645, Parliament set up the New Model Army — about 22,000 well-paid, well-trained soldiers in red coats.

For the first time, Parliament had a professional army, not just local militia.

On 14 June 1645, the New Model Army crushed Charles I's army at the Battle of Naseby in Northamptonshire.

The king's private letters were captured. They showed he had been trying to bring in foreign troops — a huge scandal.

Charles fled and surrendered to the Scots in 1646. The First Civil War was over — but the question was now what to do with the king. ❓
